diagnostic_evidence.quote: the two algorithms exhibit comparable accuracy and stability, with no single method displaying a decisive advantage in these low-dimensional regimes

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts uniform superiority of DBR over DBDP1. Tables tex2d1, tex2d2 and tex2d8 show DBDP1 with smaller mean absolute error, smaller standard deviation and smaller relative error than DBR in every row for d=1,2,8 of Example 2, and the body itself concedes there is no decisive advantage there. The evidence supports only a claim of better performance in Example 1 and at d=15,20 of Example 2.

failure_location.quote: the DBR scheme consistently outperforms the DBDP1 method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the regimes where the tables show an advantage (Example 1; Example 2 with d≥15).
issues.overall_effect: The headline comparative claim in the abstract/introduction is not supported by the reported experiments in low dimensions.
issues.title: Abstract claims DBR 'consistently outperforms' DBDP1, contradicted by the paper's own tables
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of the prose fixes the overstatement; no theorem or algorithm is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: R_{i,2}^y is defined with the exact values Y_{i+1}^{π,m,k}=u(t_{i+1},X_{i+1}^{π,m,k}) and f evaluated at the exact (Y_i^{π,m},Z_i^{π,m}), whereas the training target S_{y,i} uses the trained network NN_{y,i+1}(p_{i+1}^{m,k},θ*_{y,i+1}) and f evaluated at network outputs. Hence Y_i−S_{y,i} ≠ R_{i,2}^y (the difference contains the propagated error (1/K)Σ_k(Y_{i+1}^{π,m,k}−NN_{y,i+1}) and the f-mismatch), and likewise Z_i−S_{z,i} ≠ R_{i,2}^z. Moreover, by (NS-MC-2-1), R_{i,2}^y+R_{i,1}^y = Y_i^{π,m}−𝒴_i is the total error itself, so the theorem's right-hand side dominates N·Σ_i E|Y_i^π−𝒴_i|^2 and the stated estimate is essentially tautological rather than an error bound in terms of algorithmic (regression/Monte-Carlo) residuals.

failure_location.quote: From (\ref{NS-DMC}) and the definition of $S_{y,i}\left(p_{i}^{m}, X_{i+1}^{\pi,m} \right)$, we have

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine R_{i,2}^y := S_{y,i}(θ*)−𝒴_i and R_{i,2}^z := S_{z,i}−𝒵_i (the actual training residuals) and R_{i,1} as the Monte-Carlo errors of the network-based averages, then rework Steps 2 and 4 so that S−𝒰 is bounded through the propagated error at i+1 and the K-sample variance.
issues.overall_effect: Steps 2 and 4 of the proof are invalid as written; Theorem ae-DMCE does not deliver an error estimate in terms of quantities produced by the scheme, and the rate result thm:added-1 and the reflected version ae-DMCE-R, which reuse these steps and residuals, inherit the defect.
issues.title: Residuals R_{i,2} are defined against the exact discrete solution, so the identities E|Y_i−S_{y,i}|^2=E|R_{i,2}^y|^2 and the z-analogue are false and the bound becomes circular
issues.why_classification: A contained rewrite of two proof steps with corrected residual definitions yields a comparable error estimate; no new global architecture is needed, but the current statement/proof cannot stand.

issues.failure_explanation: In (Deep-NN-E-9-3) the difference between the K-sample average and E_i[NN_{y,i+1}] is bounded crudely by E|NN_{y,i+1}|^2 (ignoring the 1/K variance reduction), producing the constant C(1+h) in (Deep-NN-E-9-3-1); this constant is then omitted in (Deep-NN-E-10). Inserted into (Deep-NN-E-8) with the factor (1/h)Σ_i it would contribute CN^2, so the derivation cannot yield the stated bound. The same happens for Z: (Deep-NN-E-9-3-z) gives CN (also using E|NN·ΔW/h|^2 ≤ Nd E|NN|^2, which ignores that NN(p_{i+1}) depends on ΔW_i), (Deep-NN-E-9-z-1) keeps CN, but in (Deep-NN-E-16-1) the term 2h·CN = O(1) is dropped; summed over i it would give CN.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound E|(1/K)Σ_k NN(p_{i+1}^{m,k}) − E_i NN(p_{i+1}^m)|^2 = (1/K)E[Var_i NN] = O(1/K) (and O(N/K) for the ΔW/h-weighted average) using conditional independence of the K resampled increments, and absorb these into Monte-Carlo residual terms; then the (1/h)Σ_i factor gives O(N^2/K), consistent with the later choice K=O(N^3).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem ae-DMCE is invalid; with the dropped terms restored the bound diverges as N→∞. thm:added-1 and ae-DMCE-R rely on this theorem and its Steps 2–4.
issues.title: O(1) and O(N) terms produced in bounding S−𝒰 and S−𝒱 are silently dropped, so the recursion would give an O(N^2) bound
issues.why_classification: A correct but nontrivial variance computation replaces the flawed steps and yields a comparable estimate with explicit K-dependence; the result survives in recognizable form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (\ref{Deep-NN-E-r-7}) and (\ref{Deep-NN-E-r-8}) show that to achieve a convergence rate of $O(\frac{1}{N})$ in Theorem \ref{ae-DMCE},

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem ae-DMCE bounds the error by Σ_i E[N|R_{i+1,2}^y|^2+|R_{i,2}^z|^2+...], where R_{i,2} are residuals of the trained networks NN(·,θ*). The proof of thm:added-1 only establishes the best-approximation error inf_{NN∈𝒢} E|y(p_i)−NN|^2 ≤ C(R^2ε^2+(1+R^2ε^2)/R^2) for the function y_i representing 𝒰̃. No argument is given that E|R_{i,2}^y|^2 (or E|R_{i,2}^z|^2) is controlled by this infimum: this requires (at least) that θ* is the L^2-projection minimizer of the population regression loss and that E[S_{y,i}|X_i] coincides with y_i(t_i,X_i), neither of which is shown. Furthermore θ* is defined as the minimizer of the empirical loss (1/M)Σ_m obtained by SGD, so the stated bound ≤Ch, which contains no M-dependence or optimization error, cannot hold for the scheme as defined. The Monte-Carlo residual bounds E|R_{i,1}^y|^2=O(1/K), E|R_{i,1}^z|^2=O(N/K) implicit in N^2/K=O(1/N) are also asserted without proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the theorem for the population-loss minimizer over the GroupSort class, prove E|R_{i,2}|^2 ≤ inf-approximation error + Monte-Carlo variance via the L^2 projection property, and verify the O(1/K), O(N/K) variance bounds for R_{i,1}.
issues.overall_effect: The half-order convergence claim (abstract, conclusion) is not established; it depends on the unproven passage from approximation capacity to actual residuals and on an unstated population-minimizer idealization.
issues.title: Rate theorem never connects the GroupSort approximation infimum to the scheme's actual residuals R_{i,2}, and ignores empirical/SGD minimization
issues.why_classification: The missing link is a contained but nontrivial argument and requires reinterpreting θ* as an idealized minimizer; the rate itself can plausibly survive once ISSUE-002/003 are fixed.

issues.failure_explanation: In the discrete reflected scheme (NS-M-R) the continuation value at t_i is built from the reflected Y_{i+1}^π, but the auxiliary 𝒰̄_{t_i} in (Deep-NN-E-R) (and S_{y,i}, per its Section 3 definition) uses the unreflected network 𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i+1}, not 𝒴̂_{i+1}=max(𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i+1},g). Consequently (Deep-NN-E-8-R) bounds E|Ȳ_i^π−𝒴̂_i|^2 by (1+Ch)E|Y_{i+1}^π−𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i+1}|^2, a reflected-vs-unreflected discrepancy that is not the error at step i+1, so the recursion cannot be iterated. In addition, (Deep-NN-E-8-R) compares Ȳ_i^π (unreflected) with 𝒴̂_i (reflected) and (Deep-NN-E-8-R-R) bounds E|𝒴̂_i−𝒰̄_{t_i}|^2 by residuals defined for the unreflected network, while the max-Lipschitz step requires the pair (Ȳ_i^π, 𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i}); the quantities do not match. (Deep-NN-E-8-R-11) also omits the discretization term ε(h) that reappears in the statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define S_{y,i}, S_{z,i} and 𝒰̄_{t_i}, 𝒱̂_{t_i} in the RDBR scheme using the reflected value 𝒴̂_{i+1}=max(𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i+1},g); then bound E|Ȳ_i^π−𝑁𝑁̂_{y,i}|^2 (not 𝒴̂_i) by (1+Ch)E|Y_{i+1}^π−𝒴̂_{i+1}|^2 + residuals and apply |max(a,c)−max(b,c)|≤|a−b| to close the recursion.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence proof for the RDBR scheme is invalid; as specified (loss built from unreflected NN_{y,i+1}), the scheme only reflects at the current step and its analysis does not control the error of the reflected approximation.
issues.title: RDBR analysis propagates the unreflected network value and compares mismatched (reflected vs. unreflected) quantities, so the error recursion does not close
issues.why_classification: A consistent redefinition of the propagated value and a corrected recursion restore a comparable result without new global machinery, but the current proof and scheme specification are not correct.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This striking performance gap unequivocally demonstrates that the DBR algorithm retains its accuracy and stability in high-dimensional regimes

issues.failure_explanation: The relative error reported is that of the sample mean of 10 runs. At d=20 the true value is 0.259 while the standard deviation is 0.446 and the mean absolute error is 0.366 (N=90) and 0.306 (N=100), i.e. individual runs are typically off by more than 100% and the 3.7% figure results from cancellation of large positive and negative errors. At d=15, N=140 the 1.25% figure coexists with a mean absolute error of 0.225 (≈50% of |u|). The paper's claims of retained accuracy and stability (and the abstract's 'relative errors under 9.7%') are therefore not supported by the reported statistics; only a smaller bias than DBDP1 is evidenced.

failure_location.quote: DBR achieves remarkably low relative errors of $3.6974\%$, $3.3720\%$ and $9.0293\%$ under the same conditions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report and interpret the per-run error (mean absolute error / standard deviation) as the accuracy metric and restate the conclusions accordingly (e.g. reduced bias relative to DBDP1 but high variance).
issues.overall_effect: The empirical evidence for robustness of DBR at d=15,20 (a central practical claim in the abstract, introduction and conclusion of Section 5) is materially overstated.
issues.title: Claims of 'remarkably low' errors and stability at d=15,20 rest on the relative error of the 10-run mean while per-run mean absolute errors exceed the solution magnitude
issues.why_classification: Correcting the interpretation removes the advertised high-dimensional accuracy/stability claim rather than merely rewording it, though no theorem is affected.
